newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sonaca says strike jeopardises future.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sonaca says strike jeopardises future.

text.p: Belgian aeronautical firm Sonaca SA said on Friday a union strike over demands for extra cash to deal with two major orders could force the firm into bankruptcy.
Managing director Christian Jacquemain told Reuters that if unions continued a strike started on Friday, market share and revenue would be lost and "only a few days were left before bankruptcy."
A majority of the workers voted for a strike in a referendum on Thursday.
Higher than expected orders for Airbus A-320 wing parts and for parts for the 50-seat Brazilian Embraer aircraft mean Sonaca has to speed up production and restructuring in the next two years.
Sonaca, 92 percent owned by Belgium's francophone Walloon regional government, has warned that although the orderbook to date might look good, its business was highly cyclical.
